title.back: Section review: Geography and our environment

intro.source: 10 questions about Lessons 10–14. Take your time. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you like.
intro.back: 10 questions about Lessons 10-14. Take your time. You can look at the lessons again and try again as many times as you like.

questions.0.question.note: 'Thuyền dừng lại trên sông' for 'where boats stopped on a river'; check it means a landing/port to a young reader.
questions.0.question.source: Long ago, why did towns often grow at places where boats stopped on a river?
questions.0.question.back: In the old days, why did towns often grow in places where boats stopped on rivers?

questions.0.options.0.text.source: Boats kept the river from flooding
questions.0.options.0.text.back: Boats helped the river not to flood
questions.0.options.0.text.note: Review: Original read 'boats help the river not be flooded' (river as victim); English: boats kept the river from flooding. [Reviewer changed: Thuyền giúp sông không bị lũ → Thuyền ngăn sông không gây lũ]

questions.0.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Boats cannot stop a river from flooding. Towns grew where boats stopped because people could trade there. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.0.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Boats cannot stop a river from causing floods. Towns grew where boats stopped because people could trade there. Look at Lesson 10 again.

questions.0.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. Boats carried heavy goods, like grain and wood. People bought and sold these goods where the boats stopped.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. Boats carried heavy goods, like rice grain and timber. People bought and sold these goods where the boats stopped.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.note: Review: Consistency with lessons (ngũ cốc); avoids rice-specific word. [Reviewer changed: thóc và gỗ → ngũ cốc và gỗ]

questions.0.options.2.text.source: The land was high and rocky
questions.0.options.2.text.back: The land there was high and stony

questions.0.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Boats stop by the water, not on high, rocky land. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.0.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Boats stop beside the water, not on high stony land. Look at Lesson 10 again.

questions.1.stimulus.title.note: 'Made-up' is rendered as 'tự nghĩ ra' (plain, child-friendly) rather than 'hư cấu' (literary; used only in the fixed fiction label). Native speaker: choose one word and apply it across all lessons and checks. 'Riverlands' is the English map name; it is kept untranslated here, check that it matches the Vietnamese Lesson 10 map.
questions.1.stimulus.title.source: Notes from the made-up Riverlands map in Lesson 10
questions.1.stimulus.title.back: Notes from the made-up Riverlands map in Lesson 10

questions.1.stimulus.items.0.note: Site labels 'Điểm ven sông / Điểm đồi / Điểm rừng' translate 'River site / Hill site / Forest site'. They MUST match the labels in the Vietnamese Lesson 10 text and picture; adjust here if the lesson uses different words.
questions.1.stimulus.items.0.source: River site: flat land by the river. The soil is good for crops. Sometimes the river floods it.
questions.1.stimulus.items.0.back: River spot: flat land beside the river. The soil is good for crops. Sometimes the river floods here.

questions.1.stimulus.items.1.source: Hill site: high, dry ground. Floods do not reach it. The soil is thin and rocky.
questions.1.stimulus.items.1.back: Hill spot: high, dry land. Floods do not reach it. The soil is thin and stony.

questions.1.stimulus.items.2.source: Forest site: far from the river. There is wood to build with. People must cut trees before they farm.
questions.1.stimulus.items.2.back: Forest spot: far from the river. There is timber to build with. People must cut down trees before farming.

questions.1.question.source: Which fact is a good reason to build a farming town at the River site?
questions.1.question.back: Which fact is a good reason to build a farming town at the river spot?

questions.1.options.0.text.source: The soil there is good for crops.
questions.1.options.0.text.back: The soil there is good for crops.

questions.1.options.0.feedback.note: 'Phù sa' (river mud/silt) for 'mud from the river': check it is a word 10-year-olds know. | Review: English 'mud'; lesson 10 uses 'bùn'. [Reviewer changed: Phù sa → Bùn]
questions.1.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. The map says the soil at the River site is good for crops. Mud from the river makes the land fertile.
questions.1.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. The map says the soil at the river spot is good for crops. Silt from the river makes the soil fertile.

questions.1.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Floods do not reach the Hill site. But the river sometimes floods the River site. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.1.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Floods do not reach the hill spot. But sometimes the river floods at the river spot. Look at Lesson 10 again.

questions.1.options.2.text.source: There is wood to build with there.
questions.1.options.2.text.back: There is timber to build with there.

questions.1.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The wood is at the Forest site. The River site is flat land next to the river. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.1.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The timber is at the forest spot. The river spot is flat land beside the river. Look at Lesson 10 again.

questions.2.question.note: 'Chú giải' for the map key (Lesson 11 teaches it). 'Tỉ lệ' for scale on a map and 'hoa gió' for compass rose: 'hoa gió' is my choice, not in KEY_TERMS; some books say 'la bàn' or 'hoa tiêu'. Please check what Vietnamese schools use.
questions.2.question.source: Which part of a map tells you what each colour, line and shape means?
questions.2.question.back: Which part of a map tells you what each colour, line and shape means?

questions.2.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The scale helps you see how far things are in real life. Look back at Lesson 11.
questions.2.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Scale helps you know how far apart things are in real life. Look at Lesson 11 again.

questions.2.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The compass rose shows north, south, east and west. Look back at Lesson 11.
questions.2.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. A compass rose only shows north, south, east and west. Look at Lesson 11 again.

questions.2.options.2.feedback.note: The English says 'the key, or legend'. I wrote only 'Chú giải'; check whether to add 'hay bảng chú thích'. 'Kí hiệu' (spelling with i) per KEY_TERMS.
questions.2.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. The key, or legend, tells you what each symbol means. For example, a blue line can stand for a river.
questions.2.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. The key tells you what each symbol means. For example, a blue line could be a river.

questions.3.stimulus.title.note: 'Made-up' is rendered as 'tự nghĩ ra' (plain, child-friendly) rather than 'hư cấu' (literary; used only in the fixed fiction label). Native speaker: choose one word and apply it across all lessons and checks. 'Công viên Ambrey': invented name with 'Công viên' (park) translated.
questions.3.stimulus.title.source: A made-up map of Ambrey Park
questions.3.stimulus.title.back: A made-up map of Ambrey Park

questions.3.stimulus.items.1.source: The path from the gate to the pond is five squares long.
questions.3.stimulus.items.1.back: The path from the gate to the pond is five squares long.

questions.3.stimulus.items.2.note: 'B (bắc)' stands for 'N (north)': the map's letter must match the Vietnamese compass rose in Lesson 11 (Vietnamese maps use B for bắc). Check.
questions.3.stimulus.items.2.source: Compass rose: N (north) points to the top of the map
questions.3.stimulus.items.2.back: Compass rose: the letter N (north) points to the top of the map

questions.3.question.source: About how long is the path from the gate to the pond?
questions.3.question.back: About how long is the path from the gate to the pond?

questions.3.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The path is five squares long, and each square is 10 metres. Look back at Lesson 11.
questions.3.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The path is five squares long, and each square is 10 metres. Look at Lesson 11 again.

questions.3.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. Each square is 10 metres. Five squares make 50 metres.
questions.3.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. Each square is 10 metres. Five squares is 50 metres.

questions.3.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. That would be 50 squares. The path is only five squares of 10 metres each. Look back at Lesson 11.
questions.3.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. That would be 50 squares. The path is only five squares long, each 10 metres. Look at Lesson 11 again.

questions.4.question.note: Real cities. 'Thâm Quyến' is the usual Vietnamese name of Shenzhen; keep Latin 'Nairobi'. Check both.
questions.4.question.source: Nairobi and Shenzhen are two real cities. What helped both of them grow?
questions.4.question.back: Nairobi and Shenzhen are two real cities. What helped both of them grow?

questions.4.options.0.text.source: Cool weather and lots of rain
questions.4.options.0.text.back: Cool weather and lots of rain

questions.4.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Weather did not make these two cities grow. Nairobi began as a stop on a railway, and Shenzhen grew when factories opened. Look back at Lesson 12.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Weather did not make these two cities grow. Nairobi began as a stop on the railway, and Shenzhen grew when factories opened. Look at Lesson 12 again.

questions.4.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Rich soil helps farms grow crops. These two cities grew because of jobs and transport. Look back at Lesson 12.
questions.4.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Fertile soil helps farms grow crops. These two cities grew because of jobs and transport. Look at Lesson 12 again.

questions.4.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. Nairobi began as a stop on a railway, and factories opened in Shenzhen. Jobs and transport brought many people.
questions.4.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. Nairobi began as a stop on the railway, and factories opened in Shenzhen. Jobs and transport brought many people.

questions.5.stimulus.title.note: 'Made-up' is rendered as 'tự nghĩ ra' (plain, child-friendly) rather than 'hư cấu' (literary; used only in the fixed fiction label). Native speaker: choose one word and apply it across all lessons and checks.

questions.5.stimulus.body.note: Ostrin is invented, kept. 'Tuyến tàu hỏa' for train line.
questions.5.stimulus.body.source: A new train line opens in the made-up town of Ostrin. A factory opens next to the station, with 600 new jobs. Five years later, twice as many people live in Ostrin. But the town still has only one small school.
questions.5.stimulus.body.back: A new train line opens in Ostrin, a made-up town. A factory opens next to the station, with 600 new jobs. Five years later, twice as many people live in Ostrin. But the town still has only one small school.

questions.5.question.source: What problem is Ostrin most likely to have?
questions.5.question.back: What problem is Ostrin likely to have?

questions.5.options.0.text.source: The one school gets very crowded.

questions.5.options.0.feedback.note: 'Khi dân số tăng, các dịch vụ cũng cần tăng theo' (service per KEY_TERMS 'dịch vụ'): check it is clear for a school as a service.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. The number of people grew fast, but the school did not. A service needs to grow when the population grows.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. The number of people grew fast but the school did not. When the population grows, services also need to grow.

questions.5.options.1.text.source: There are fewer jobs in the town.
questions.5.options.1.text.back: The town has fewer jobs than before.

questions.5.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The factory brought 600 new jobs, so there are more jobs, not fewer. Look back at Lesson 12.
questions.5.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The factory brought 600 new jobs, so there are more jobs, not fewer. Look at Lesson 12 again.

questions.5.options.2.text.source: It is hard to get to other towns.
questions.5.options.2.text.back: It is hard to travel to faraway towns.

questions.5.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The new train line makes travel easier. Think about the school instead. Look back at Lesson 12.
questions.5.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The new train line made travel easier. Think about the school. Look at Lesson 12 again.

questions.6.stimulus.title.note: 'Made-up' is rendered as 'tự nghĩ ra' (plain, child-friendly) rather than 'hư cấu' (literary; used only in the fixed fiction label). Native speaker: choose one word and apply it across all lessons and checks.

questions.6.stimulus.body.source: Kelmar is a made-up town. For the last 40 years, its summers have been hot and dry. Most of its rain has fallen in winter. Today, a cool wind is blowing, and grey clouds cover the sky.
questions.6.stimulus.body.back: Kelmar is a made-up town. For the past 40 years, summers here are hot and dry. Most rain falls in winter. Today a cool wind is blowing and grey clouds cover the sky.

questions.6.question.note: Weather = 'thời tiết', climate = 'khí hậu', pattern = 'mẫu hình'. Check that learners can tell them apart.
questions.6.question.source: Which one is about weather, not climate?
questions.6.question.back: Which sentence is about weather, not climate?

questions.6.options.0.text.source: Summers are usually hot and dry.
questions.6.options.0.text.back: Summers are usually very hot and dry.

questions.6.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. This is a pattern over many years, so it is climate. Weather is what the air is like now. Look back at Lesson 13.
questions.6.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. This is a pattern over many years, so it is climate. Weather is what the air is like right now. Look at Lesson 13 again.

questions.6.options.1.text.source: A cool wind is blowing today.
questions.6.options.1.text.back: Today a cool wind is blowing.

questions.6.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. This is about one day, and it can change fast. That makes it weather.
questions.6.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. This sentence is about one day, and it can change very fast. So it is weather.

questions.6.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. This is what usually happens each year, so it is climate. Weather is what the air is like now. Look back at Lesson 13.
questions.6.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. This is what usually happens each year, so it is climate. Weather is what the air is like right now. Look at Lesson 13 again.

questions.7.question.note: 'Đường xích đạo'. Check season names; near the equator there are 'mùa mưa' and 'mùa khô'.
questions.7.question.source: What are the seasons like near the equator?
questions.7.question.back: What are the seasons like near the equator?

questions.7.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Many places far from the equator have these four seasons. Look back at Lesson 13.
questions.7.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Many places far from the equator have these four seasons. Look at Lesson 13 again.

questions.7.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Places near the equator are warm all year. Look back at Lesson 13.
questions.7.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Places near the equator are warm all year. Look at Lesson 13 again.

questions.7.options.2.text.source: A rainy season and a dry season
questions.7.options.2.text.back: One rainy season and one dry season

questions.7.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. Near the equator, it is warm all year. So the seasons are usually rainy or dry.
questions.7.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. Near the equator it is warm all year. So the seasons are usually a rainy season or a dry season.

questions.8.stimulus.title.note: 'Made-up' is rendered as 'tự nghĩ ra' (plain, child-friendly) rather than 'hư cấu' (literary; used only in the fixed fiction label). Native speaker: choose one word and apply it across all lessons and checks. Brookside kept.
questions.8.stimulus.title.source: The made-up town of Brookside from Lesson 14: three ideas for a low bridge
questions.8.stimulus.title.back: The made-up town of Brookside in Lesson 14: three ideas for a low bridge

questions.8.stimulus.items.0.source: The problem: heavy rain sometimes covers the low footbridge with water.
questions.8.stimulus.items.0.back: Problem: heavy rain sometimes covers the low footbridge with water.

questions.8.stimulus.items.1.note: 'Biển cảnh báo' for 'warning sign'. Check whether the Vietnamese Lesson 14 uses 'cảnh báo' (alert) consistently.
questions.8.stimulus.items.1.source: Idea A: put a warning sign by the bridge. It is cheap and quick.
questions.8.stimulus.items.1.back: Idea A: put a warning sign next to the bridge. This is cheap and fast.

questions.8.stimulus.items.2.source: Idea B: build the bridge higher and add a ramp. It costs more and takes months.
questions.8.stimulus.items.2.back: Idea B: build a higher bridge and add a ramp. This costs more money and takes a few months.

questions.8.stimulus.items.3.source: Idea C: send phone messages and put up paper notices when heavy rain is coming.
questions.8.stimulus.items.3.back: Idea C: send phone messages and put up paper notices when heavy rain is coming.

questions.8.question.source: What is one problem with Idea A, the warning sign?
questions.8.question.back: What is one problem with Idea A, the sign?

questions.8.options.0.text.source: It does not make the bridge safer.
questions.8.options.0.text.back: It does not make the bridge safer.

questions.8.options.0.feedback.note: The English ends with 'some people cannot read the sign'; kept as 'có người không đọc được biển'. Check it is tactful.
questions.8.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. A sign is quick and cheap, but the bridge stays low. Also, some people cannot read the sign.
questions.8.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. A sign is fast and cheap, but the bridge is still low. Also, some people cannot read the sign.

questions.8.options.1.text.source: It costs a lot and takes months.
questions.8.options.1.text.back: It costs a lot of money and takes a few months.

questions.8.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. That is Idea B, raising the bridge. A sign is cheap and quick. Look back at Lesson 14.
questions.8.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. That is Idea B, raising the bridge. A sign is cheap and fast. Look at Lesson 14 again.

questions.8.options.2.text.source: Everyone needs a phone to see it.
questions.8.options.2.text.back: Everyone needs a phone to see it.

questions.8.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Phone messages are part of Idea C. A sign stands by the bridge, so no phone is needed. Look back at Lesson 14.
questions.8.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Phone messages are part of Idea C. A sign stands next to the bridge, so it needs no phone. Look at Lesson 14 again.

questions.9.question.note: 'Sự hòa nhập' for 'inclusion': my choice, not in KEY_TERMS. Alternative 'sự bao gồm', 'sự không bỏ ai lại phía sau'. Native speaker please decide. 'Cảnh báo' for 'alert'.
questions.9.question.source: A made-up library puts its signs in three languages and adds pictures. Now everyone can find what they need. What is this an example of?
questions.9.question.back: A made-up library writes its signs in three languages and adds pictures. Now everyone can find what they need. What is this an example of?

questions.9.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. An alert is a message that warns people about danger. These signs help people find things. Look back at Lesson 14.
questions.9.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. A warning is a message telling everyone about danger. These signs help everyone find things. Look at Lesson 14 again.

questions.9.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The environment is the land, water, air, plants and animals around us. Look back at Lesson 14.
questions.9.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The environment is the land, water, air, plants and animals around us. Look at Lesson 14 again.

questions.9.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. Inclusion means making sure everyone can take part. Signs in three languages, with pictures, help more people.
questions.9.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. Inclusion means making sure everyone can take part. Signs in three languages with pictures help more people.

results.high.source: Well done. You know a lot about places, maps and how people live with their environment.
results.high.back: Well done. You know a lot about places, maps and how people live with their environment.

results.middle.source: Good work. You got many questions right. Look back at the lessons for the ones you missed, and try again if you like.
results.middle.back: Good. You answered many correctly. Look at the lessons again for the ones not right, and try again if you like.
